chapter: Louis Metcalf and leading his own bands
title: His feature numbers and the leader as announcer
summary: He featured ballads such as Stardust and swing choruses, and acted as announcer who let the soloists do their thing.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: : But I mean you would -- what would you play for your feature?
Well, I -- sometime different solos (unintelligible) like (unintelligible) the Waterfront, like, for instance, 'Stardust.'
: Yeah, you'd sort of do a ballad --
: -- like the sort of Coleman Hawkins thing had been established by then.
Right. Then what we -- four or five choruses on -- like swing too, they'd get in tempo, you know.
: I mean, you know, the reason I'm asking this is that at this time -- by this time the leaders, you know, thing changed a bit. The leaders were like the stars.
: You know, I mean at one time, I mean, Paul Whiteman waved (unintelligible) and so forth, but now the leaders, the Benny Goodmans and people were out front mostly.
Because I got out and played with a

six piece -- I call them a tenor part. Then, like with those big dancers, I'm going to feature, I call, and I would be featuring a particular one by trumpet player, so and so and so, a trombone player, Dickie Wells, Stretch tenor player. I was announcer. Let the men do their thing.
Well, I mean as long as they can be -- if they can solo in an interesting way, it makes sense.
